title: Operation-time policy reevaluation
outOfScope: Provider configuration, Branch Protection, and external production operations.
Executing scripts, API writes, releases, migrations, or destructive operations.
Immutable archive evidence except through the governed archive command.

sources.reason: Authoritative WI-06 requirements and acceptance criteria supplied by the user.
Existing deterministic trust and provenance policy seam extended by WI-05.
Existing regression suite and coverage association for the policy module.

riskAssessment.reason: Operation-time decisions can otherwise reuse stale approval or be bypassed by an actual tool call that differs from the reviewed request.

reasons: Code, tests, and synchronized public documentation change together; no external provider validation is in scope.

executionDecision.reason: User authorized governed Contract writes and the complete Work Item lifecycle; this Work Item implements a local policy model only.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A requested operation is re-evaluated against the actual tool call, target resource, current authority, evidence freshness, and destructive impact immediately before execution.
A later dangerous-script execution is blocked or requires a new review even when the earlier step only created the script.
An approval binding is invalid when its target resource or declared scope differs from the operation-time request.
Stale evidence yields human confirmation rather than automatic execution.
An actual tool call that does not match the original request is stopped with a specific recovery condition.
All listed high-risk operation categories are represented by deterministic regression coverage.
A focused English, Chinese, and Japanese reference page names the policy inputs and states that the model does not execute external operations.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.

intent.problem: Input-time trust checks alone do not prevent later scripts, tools, or multi-step tasks from changing the operation or target after an earlier request was approved.
constraints: Keep the model deterministic and fail closed; it must decide policy only and never execute an operation.
Do not modify provider configuration or make external production claims.
Preserve WI-05 provenance and use current, attributable authority/evidence for every operation-time decision.
Keep public policy APIs documented and covered by focused regressions.
intent.rationale: A local, explicit operation-time policy record makes changed scope, stale evidence, and request/tool mismatches reviewable before a high-risk action can proceed.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: User explicitly authorized required Contract and governed Work Item writes for this and future Work Items.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff and restore related tests and docs.
rawUserRequest: Implement WI-06 operation-time-policy-reevaluation from the supplied AI Cockpit comprehensive remediation instructions; user authorized governed Contract writes and requested sequential completion through archive, PR, merge, and branch cleanup.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: dangerous script execution is re-evaluated after script creation
scenarioCoverage.expected: the actual execution is blocked or sent to review independently of the earlier create-script step

scenarioCoverage.scenario: approval binding becomes invalid when scope or target changes
scenarioCoverage.expected: changed scope or resource cannot reuse a former approval

scenarioCoverage.scenario: stale evidence and request/tool mismatch stop automatic execution
scenarioCoverage.expected: stale evidence requires human confirmation and mismatched calls are blocked with recovery guidance
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run freshness and actual-call mismatch regressions across all required high-risk categories.
